Request reprint permissions here.Over the past year, the world’s attention has turned to economic chokepoints—with good reason. Iran has exercised its control over the Strait of Hormuz to gum up the global economy, and China has used its command over critical minerals to gain leverage in trade negotiations. Less consideration, however, has been paid to chokepoints in the digital domain, which could prove just as treacherous.Chinese hackers have gained and retained access to U.S. communications, energy, and transportation infrastructure.
